A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 24-page versions of the same ADAPT work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–B support reliable textual and visual comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ADAPT classification experiments in Section 4, with additional statistical checks, backbone comparisons, ablations and robustness results in Appendices A.4 and B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices A.4 and B.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix A retain the same Gaussian classifier, knowledge-bank construction, regularized objectives, mean/covariance estimates and closed-form online/transductive inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same natural distribution shifts, ImageNet-C corruptions and ten fine-grained datasets. The appendix few-shot and low-confidence scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including Tables 2–4, 12–14 and the CLIP/TDA robustness comparison in Table 16.

E3.justification: Both retain online batch size 1, full-test-set transduction, alpha 0.9 and knowledge-bank sizes 16/6. Backbone configurations, shot counts, corruption severity levels and other appendix evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: The same component ablations, hyperparameter and initialization analyses, input-order tests and iterative-versus-closed-form comparisons remain. Appendix normality, covariance, corruption-severity and scarce-confidence analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 retains 100 repetitions of random feature projection and the same Henze–Zirkler/Shapiro–Wilk p-value reporting in Table 10. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, ADAPT's online/transductive averages remain 66.53/67.09 in Table 2, 28.56/30.29 in Table 3 and 70.76/72.43 in Table 4; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same mathematical definitions, Gaussian/shared-covariance assumptions, objectives and derivations. Differences in mathematical typesetting do not alter the formulas or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about distribution-aware, source-free, backpropagation-free adaptation, online/transductive applicability, robustness and efficiency.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A.4/B.4 retain the same Gaussian-model limitations, explanations of covariance sparsity and sample exclusion, and qualifications concerning low-confidence streams and delayed adaptation.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, hyperparameters, NVIDIA RTX A6000 hardware information and the project link are unchanged. No technical instructions or resource-access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 72 works and retain the same research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix A.4. Bibliography entries move across pages without changes to cited-work membership.

P1.justification: v3 updates Youngeun Kim's affiliation from Yale to Amazon, adds a prior-employment footnote and funding acknowledgement, and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is re-exported as a raster image with a different cat example and lighter labels/lines, while retaining its structure and meaning. Minor spacing changes and acknowledgement-driven bibliography reflow occur; other figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same methods, proofs, experimental evidence, interpretations and limitations. The publication, affiliation and funding updates and limited Figure 1 redesign produce no meaningful net change in scientific rigor, reproducibility or explanatory quality.
